record.original_question: Consider a two-phase composite in two spatial dimensions in which phase 1 occupies volume fraction f, the right-hand fields are n-tuples of fields each equal to a constant real 2-vector plus the gradient of a scalar periodic potential, the left-hand fields are n-tuples of divergence-free fields, and the constitutive law is J(x)=L(x)E(x) with L(x)=chi(x)L_1+[1-chi(x)]L_2. Is the G_f-closure of all achievable effective tensors L* equal to the closure obtained using only multiple-rank laminate microstructures, for every positive integer n?

evidence.quote: Problem 2: For two-phase composites in two spatial dimensions, such that phase 1 occupies a volume fraction f, is the Gf -closure equal to its lamination closure when the fields on the right of the constitutive law have n components, each being the sum of a real 2 component vector and the gradient of a scalar periodic potential, while the fields on the left of the constitutive law also have n components, each having zero divergence, in which n is an arbitrary positive integer?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a volume fraction $f\in(0,1)$. Let $L_1, L_2$ be two given constant symmetric positive-definite tensors mapping $(\mathbb{R}^2)^n	o(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$. For a measurable indicator function $\chi:\mathbb{T}^2	o\{0,1\}$ (defined on the 2-dimensional torus, i.e.\ $\mathbb{Z}^2$-periodic on $\mathbb{R}^2$) with $\int_{\mathbb{T}^2}\chi=f$, define $L(x)=\chi(x)L_1+(1-\chi(x))L_2$.

Consider periodic field pairs $(E,J)$ where $E=(E_1,\dots,E_n)$ and $J=(J_1,\dots,J_n)$ with each $E_i,J_i:\mathbb{T}^2	o\mathbb{R}^2$, satisfying:
  (i) $E_i(x)=e_i+
abla\varphi_i(x)$ for some constant vector $e_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and some scalar periodic potential $\varphi_i$;
  (ii) $
abla\cdot J_i=0$ in the periodic sense;
  (iii) the constitutive law $J(x)=L(x)E(x)$ holds a.e.

The effective tensor $L^*$ is the constant tensor characterized by $\langle Jangle = L^*\langle Eangle$, where $\langle\cdotangle$ denotes the average over $\mathbb{T}^2$, taken over all admissible $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$. Let $G_f(L_1,L_2)$ be the closure (in the natural topology on tensors) of the set of all $L^*$ achievable via such measurable $\chi$ with mean $f$.

Let $G_f^L(L_1,L_2)$ be the analogous closure restricted to microstructures $\chi$ obtained as multiple-rank (hierarchical) laminates of phases $L_1$ and $L_2$ with overall volume fraction $f$ of phase 1.

Question: Is $G_f(L_1,L_2)=G_f^L(L_1,L_2)$ for every positive integer $n$ and every choice of $L_1,L_2,f$ as above?
artifact.status_search_result: This is one of Milton's stated open problems on the theory of composites (2020/2021). Surveys describe it as open: it is not known in general whether the G_f-closure of two-phase 2D composites coincides with its lamination (hierarchical multiple-rank laminate) closure for arbitrary n. No solution has been reported in the search results.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in the theory of composites
status_evidence.snippet: The central question is whether two-dimensional, two-phase composites with general geometries have the same set of possible effective tensors as those of hierarchical laminates.
status_evidence.claim: The equality of G-closure and lamination closure for 2D two-phase composites is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.claim: Posed as an open problem for arbitrary positive integer n.
